findings.source_claim: cl_D(I)_+={a in A_+: a triangleleft b for some b in I_+}.

counterexample.ideal: I=fA, f(t)=t for t>=0 and f(t)=it for t<0
counterexample.K: continuous g with |g(t)|<=C|t| for some finite C

assumptions_checked: A is a unital commutative C*-algebra
I additive, complex-linear and two-sided; no self-adjointness assumption is allowed by Theorem 4.4
I_+=I intersection A_+ as explicitly defined
J and K positively spanned and hereditary; strong invariance automatic in commutative algebra
triangleleft is exactly domination by a positive integer multiple in this algebra
findings.decisive_proof: If g=fh>=0 and h continuous, right values h(t)=g(t)/t are nonnegative real and left values h(t)=i*g(t)/|t| are positive imaginary. Continuity forces h(0)=0, so I_+=J_+. Conversely every g in J_+ has quotient g/f continuous by zero. Thus claimed RHS=J_+. Any Dixmier L containing I positively spans f and hence heredity gives |f|<=sum |c_j|b_j in L; this forces all K in L. K itself contains I and is Dixmier, so cl_D(I)=K. The witness |t| is in K_+ but not J_+.

counterevidence_and_limits: The squeezing theorem remains true for this example.
No counterexample to Theorem 5.2 or the main equivalence is claimed.

repair.status: local general repair verified under earlier results
repair.argument: For every Dixmier L, Theorem 3.9 and Proposition 3.10 give x in L iff |x| in L. Therefore cl_D(I)_+ is generated as a strongly invariant order ideal by all |x|, x in I, and equals {a: a triangleleft sum_j |x_j| for a finite family in I}. Proposition 2.8 and Lemma 2.7 give a^(1+eps) triangleleft (sum |x_j|)^(1+eps) triangleleft sum |x_j|^(1+eps). The first part of Theorem 4.4, already established using Lemma 4.3, puts every summand in int_D(I)_+. This proves the squeeze; delta follows by eps=(1-delta)^(-1)-1.
repair.boundary: Repairs this bridge without strengthening its hypotheses; does not independently certify every earlier external input or the whole paper.

independent_verification.assumptions: A=C([-1,1]) is a unital commutative C*-algebra; f(t)=t for t>=0 and it for t<0 is continuous; I=fA is a two-sided complex-linear ideal. The source allows arbitrary ring ideals without closedness or self-adjointness, so this example meets rather than strengthens the hypotheses. In this algebra x*x=xx*, making a triangleleft b equivalent to a<=m b for some positive integer m.
independent_verification.independent_proof: Put J={g:o(|t|)} and K={g:|g|<=C|t|}; sums and bounded multipliers preserve both bounds, and positive/negative real/imaginary parts give positive spanning. Heredity holds, and strong invariance is automatic in the commutative algebra. For g=fh>=0, h(t)=g(t)/t lies on the nonnegative real ray on the right and h(t)=i g(t)/|t| lies on the nonnegative imaginary ray on the left. Continuity forces h(0)=0 and g=o(|t|). Conversely every nonnegative g=o(|t|) has continuous quotient g/f extended by zero. Hence I_+=J_+ and the claimed RHS is J_+. K is Dixmier and contains I, so cl_D(I) subset K. Any Dixmier L containing f positively spans f=sum c_j b_j; |f|<=sum |c_j|b_j and heredity put |f|=|t| in L. Positive spanning then puts K in L. Thus cl_D(I)=K, while |t| is in K_+ and not J_+. This is an exact infinite-dimensional proof, independent of finite diagnostics.
independent_verification.counterevidence: The example satisfies int_D(I)=J because every Dixmier ideal inside I is spanned by I_+=J_+, and J subset I. K^(1+epsilon) subset J for every epsilon>0, so the squeezing conclusion survives. The notation I_+=I intersection A_+ is explicit, ruling out a hidden reinterpretation as all moduli; |f|/f has different one-sided limits 1 and i, so |f| is not in I.
independent_verification.impact: Theorem 5.2 begins with the squeeze and uses it in central semiprime/idempotent implications. The false equality is consequently a demonstrated core derivation defect. A local repair and absence of a main-theorem counterexample do not automatically reduce its severity.
independent_verification.repair: For any Dixmier L, Theorem 3.9 and Proposition 3.10 applied to L^2 give x in L iff |x| in L. Thus cl_D(I)_+ is the strongly invariant order ideal generated by all |x| with x in I, equivalently {a>=0:a triangleleft sum_j |x_j| for a finite family in I}. Proposition 2.8 and Lemma 2.7 imply a^(1+epsilon) triangleleft (sum_j |x_j|)^(1+epsilon) triangleleft sum_j |x_j|^(1+epsilon). The already proved first part of Theorem 4.4 puts each summand in int_D(I)_+; hereditary strong invariance gives the desired squeeze. Taking epsilon=(1-delta)^(-1)-1 and the (1-delta)-power proves the other side. The finite sum must be retained.
independent_verification.repair_limits: Relevant preceding comparison and power statements and their uses were read and checked on pp.7-15. The repair is conditional on that preceding theory and its external inputs; no whole-paper proof certificate or author adoption is claimed.
